subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Five-Year Plan Myth
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Five-Year Plan Myth.

hook.text: Reid Hoffman, LinkedIn's founder, says rigid five-year plans are useless in a world that changes every twelve months.

buildup.text: The economy shifts, industries emerge, and roles disappear. A fixed plan becomes outdated before it starts.

discovery.text: Think in 18-month cycles. Each cycle has a theme: build a skill, grow a network, or ship a visible project.

twist.text: Direction matters more than a destination. Knowing you want to lead is more useful than naming the exact role.

climax.text: Plan your next 18 months with one clear goal. Revisit and adjust as the landscape shifts. Stay flexible.

punchline.text: Eighteen months, one clear goal. Then reassess.

quiz.question: Why do rigid five-year career plans often fail?
options: People lack the discipline to follow them
Industries change faster than long-range plans can adapt
Five years is too short to achieve meaningful goals
